== Biography ==
Patrick Glasgow (recorded as Patrike) was christened on '''4 August 1667''' in Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland. His father was recorded as James Glasgow<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTBS-98C : 16 September 2021), Patrike Glasgow, christened 4 Aug 1667, Gordon, Berwickshire, Scotland. Father: James Glasgow.</ref>.

Patrick married [[Fairburn-170|Helen Fairbairn]] (also spelled Fairbarne). Their marriage appears to be recorded twice in 1707, likely representing proclamations (banns) and the marriage ceremony in different parishes associated with the couple:
* Marriage recorded on '''23 May 1707''' in Stitchel, Roxburghshire<ref>"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYQ1-96T : 11 February 2020), Patrick Glasgow marriage to Helen Fairbairn, 23 May 1707, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland.</ref>.
* Marriage recorded on '''1 July 1707''' in Eccles, Berwickshire<ref>"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTL4-LPT : 11 February 2020), Patrick Glasgow marriage to Helen Fairbarne, 1 Jul 1707, Eccles, Berwickshire, Scotland.</ref>.

By 1708, Patrick and Helen were residing in Stitchel, Roxburghshire, where they had several children christened:
* John Glasgow, christened 2 May 1708<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMW-9QT : 16 September 2021), Patrick Glasgow in entry for John Glasgow, christened 2 May 1708, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: Patrick Glasgow, Helen Fairbairn.</ref>.
* Agnes Glasgow, christened 31 July 1709<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X111-P2H : 16 September 2021), Patrick Glasgow in entry for Agnes Glasgow, christened 31 Jul 1709, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: Patrick Glasgow, Helen Fairbairn.</ref>.
* [[Glasgow-1238|James Glasgow]] (Glasow), christened 11 May 1712<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMM7-GMJ : 16 September 2021), Patrick Glasow in entry for James Glasow, christened 11 May 1712, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: Patrick Glasow, Helen Fairbarn.</ref>. (Note: This link connects to the next generation).
* Isobell Glasgow (Glascow), christened 10 August 1716<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMM-S4Y : 16 September 2021), Patrick Glascow in entry for Isobell Glascow, christened 10 Aug 1716, Stitchel, Roxburghshire, Scotland. Parents: Patrick Glascow, Helen Fairbarn.</ref>.

Patrick must have been alive in late 1715 or early 1716 for Isobell to be conceived and born. His date of death requires confirmation from reliable records.

== Research Notes ==
=== Stichill family and court records, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1440|Patrick Glasgow]] of [[Glasgow-1238|James Glasgow]] is now assessed 92% confident, from 86% probable. The 1712 Stichill James, explicitly indexed as Patrick Glasow and Helen Fairbarn’s son, is confidently inferred to be the James who married Elizabath Tait in the same parish in January 1740. An age of about 28, continuity in this small local surname family and the later household’s son Patrick (1742) and daughter Helen (1750), repeating both proposed paternal grandparents’ names, form a combined identity argument. Naming is supporting evidence rather than a mandatory rule or independent proof of each step. The specific Patrick/Helen household is independently established by their 1707 marriage entries and 1708–1716 children. Newly inspected printed court minutes place Patrick at Stichill in 1712 and appoint him a burlaw man in 1715; these add local continuity, not a father clause. The unsupported Uphall field is not a competing contemporary record. No concrete rival Stichill James family has been identified in the held material; this is not an exhaustive population search.

Newly checked printed court records: 8 November 1712, Patrick Glasgow in Stitchill was fined one shilling sterling for reclaiming his impounded horse; 10 December 1715, he was appointed one of five burlaw men. The 13 November 1739 body names Peter Glasgow, fined with two other men over carrying teind peas; the edition’s index groups this under Patrick. Retain that last identification as a compatible continuation, not a certain death/survival boundary. The manuscript court book was not inspected. These records concern the local Stichill adult, not independent identification of the 1667 Gordon child.<ref>[https://ia800706.us.archive.org/9/items/recordsofbaronco00sticrich/recordsofbaronco00sticrich.pdf#page=211 George Gunn (ed.), Records of the Baron Court of Stichill 1655–1807 (1905), act 111, printed pp. 166–167/PDF 210–211]; [https://ia800706.us.archive.org/9/items/recordsofbaronco00sticrich/recordsofbaronco00sticrich.pdf#page=216 George Gunn (ed.), Records of the Baron Court of Stichill 1655–1807 (1905), act 117, printed p. 172/PDF 216]; [https://ia800706.us.archive.org/9/items/recordsofbaronco00sticrich/recordsofbaronco00sticrich.pdf#page=240 George Gunn (ed.), Records of the Baron Court of Stichill 1655–1807 (1905), act 158, printed pp. 196–197/PDF 240–241; index p. 241/PDF 285]. Printed pages visually checked 22 October 2026; original manuscript unread.</ref>

92% is a subjective confident inference for James’s father Patrick in the Stichill Patrick/Helen household, including the 1712-child/1740-husband identification. The underlying parish images and the FamilySearch 1742 page were not newly inspected; a security challenge blocked the latter. Patrick’s identification with the 1667 Gordon child, the 1765 Swinton couple, the Leitholm Robert hypothesis and all mothers retain their separate assessments. No birth, death, place, spouse, parent selection or identity merge changes. The new court pages establish recorded acts, not biological kinship. WikiTree’s father control was checked on 22 October 2026 and was already confident; no new live certainty mark is pending.

Next useful test: Check the original 1712 child and 1740 marriage for residence, relatives or occupation; test the 1765 Swinton household separately. Seek a title or probate link for the older Gordon identity rather than repeating this now-confident local father inference.

This changes a local assessment, not an attachment or the already-confident live father control.


=== Gordon household review — 17 October 2026 ===

'''Gordon household review, 17 October 2026:''' James is the documented father in the Gordon child entry; Agnes Watt is the probable mother through the 1663 Polwarth marriage and the six-child family sequence. Later adult identifications retain their previous assessment.

Prefer one household: James Glasgow, indexed with Agnes Waitte at Polwarth on 18 June 1663, is probably the James who fathered the Gordon children John (1666), Patrike (1667), Jean (1671), Robert (1673), Agnes (1676) and Margrat (1679). The father’s repeated full name, the neighbouring Berwickshire parishes, the first child three years after marriage and the orderly thirteen-year child sequence form a coherent family. The daughter Agnes supplies modest naming support; it is not the deciding evidence. The maintained 1702 Gordon marriage citation for Jean also names father James, adding a compatible adult continuation for her. Read together, these favour a single local family over six isolated fathers or an unrelated Polwarth couple. No concrete competing contemporary Gordon James household has been identified in the maintained material. That is the scope of this comparison, not a claim to have exhausted the population.

The child indexes explicitly name James as father but omit the mother. Their named-father roles are documented for the record-defined children; identifying that father with the 1663 Polwarth husband is probable. Agnes Watt is separately assessed as probable mother of all six children on the marriage, locality and sustained family sequence. This is an inference, not literal maternity in the indexes; a later marriage or another local James remains possible. Jean’s later marriage and the later adult identities of John and Patrick remain separately assessed. Patrick’s proposed Kilclone son and migration, James’s own John Glasgow-1084 ancestry and the unrelated Kilwaughter James are not strengthened. No original register image was newly inspected: this review combines the previously accepted index entries and maintained citations.

The cited Gordon index dates are retained separately from the profile date and place fields. John’s Duns attribution needs comparison with the Gordon baptism citation; Patrick’s 8 April date differs from the 4 August index, and Robert’s 4 January date differs from the 1 April index. These discrepancies require the original entries. The indexes do not by themselves establish exact birth dates. James’s own parents and the later adult identities and migrations of the children remain separate questions.

=== Earlier maintained research retained ===

The dated Gordon household review gives the current conclusion; earlier material remains available below.

=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1440|Patrick / Patrike Glasgow of Gordon]], represented by the Gordon Patrike baptism of 1667, is selected as a very uncertain working father of [[Glasgow-3920|Patrick Glasco of the Kilclone memorial]] of the Kilclone memorial. The memorial’s age 60 at death in May 1754 puts the younger Patrick’s birth around 1694. If the Gordon baptism was near birth, the older Patrick would have been about 27 then: an ordinary father–son interval. The matching Patrick/Patrike and Glasgow/Glasco name pair supplies a specific older candidate rather than an invented ancestor. This is a very weak generational model; neither name recurrence nor a feasible age establishes paternity. There is no reviewed deed, parish entry, probate clause, occupation or shared associate connecting Gordon or Stitchel to Kilclone. No migration or Scottish birthplace is newly established for the Meath man, and the catalogue is not a complete census of older Patricks.

The Gordon profile also gathers Patrick’s marriage entries with Helen Fairbairn/Fairbarne at Stitchel on 23 May 1707 and Eccles on 1 July 1707, followed by children in 1708–1716. Those adult events do not themselves identify the groom with the 1667 child. If that combined identity is correct, the proposed Meath son would predate the recorded 1707 marriage by about 13 years. Helen is therefore not selected as his mother. No earlier wife, earlier marriage, illegitimacy, second household or move is invented. The proposed father would require an unrecorded earlier child, and that is a real weakness of the model. The two 1707 dates remain separate recorded entries; their precise banns/ceremony relationship has not been newly checked. The supplied Gordon index reads 4 August 1667 while the structured birth field says 8 April 1667. This existing day/month conflict remains visible, and neither index is used as proof of an exact birthday.

The model keeps the two Patricks distinct. A man baptised in 1667 would have been at least about 86–87 in 1754, incompatible with the Kilclone memorial’s age 60 unless the memorial age is substantially wrong. No evidence justifies correcting that age by a generation. A father–son hypothesis fits the two dated accounts better than identifying them as one person, but another father or more distant relationship remains possible. The 1667 index names James as father of the Gordon child, not a father for the Meath Patrick. The modern [[Glasgow-3107|Glasgow-3107]] identification and the Gordon account’s existing maternal and ancestral attachments retain their previous qualifications; this new edge does not independently prove them. The project’s reported Y-DNA affinity does not provide a named parent or establish that this particular untested Meath family belongs to a tested line.

The Kilclone inscription identifies Patrick as James’s father, and Richard and William as James’s brothers. Richard and William died on 1 November 1738; Richard’s age is 10 and William’s is printed with a query at about 7. Patrick died in May 1754 aged 60. These statements define the existing nuclear family and remain separate from the new proposed grandfather. The source used is a modern reproduction of a transcription reported in 1892, not a newly inspected photograph of the stone. The inscription supplies no mother, wife, occupation, birthplace or Scottish origin. Kilclone is the memorial context, not independent proof of Patrick’s birthplace or exact place of death. No parent-child confidence grade within the memorial family is changed.

One very uncertain father is newly selected, with no mother. This is a speculative working family connection, not a proved Scotland–Meath migration or an identity merge. The age 60 memorial reading, pre 1707 child problem, uncertain adult identity of the Scottish Patrick and all prior source limitations remain explicit. * '''Father Confirmed:''' Patrick's father is confirmed as James Glasgow via Patrick's 1667 christening record. Further research is needed to identify this James Glasgow (potentially [[Glasgow-3107|James Glasgow (1653-)]]?, whose own details need verification).
* '''Dual Marriage Records:''' The two marriage records from 1707 in Eccles (Berwickshire) and Stitchel (Roxburghshire) likely represent the intention/banns and the ceremony, or recordings in both home parishes. This is common in Scottish records.
* '''Death Date Conflict:''' The christening of daughter Isobell in August 1716 indicates Patrick was alive in late 1715/early 1716. This contradicts any unsourced death dates around 1712 sometimes seen in online trees (like the summary for PID MSQL-2CS mentioned previously). Patrick's actual death date/record needs to be found.
* '''Geographic Path:''' Patrick was christened in Gordon (Berwickshire), married in Eccles (Berwickshire)/Stitchel (Roxburghshire), and settled in Stitchel (Roxburghshire) where his known children were christened.
* '''Irrelevant Attached Source:''' A source for a "Patrick Young" (FamilySearch record XT1H-JMS) was found attached to Patrick Glasgow's profile on FamilySearch (as of analysis date) but appears unrelated and should be disregarded unless relevance can be proven.

Information requires independent verification from primary sources.)</ref> with caution, always seeking primary source verification.
* '''Death/Burial Records Needed:''' Records confirming the death or burial dates and places for both Patrick Glasgow and Helen Fairbairn are needed. Likely search areas include Stitchel or surrounding parishes after 1716.
